dismissed.label: Docket process
dismissed.why: The Docket's processor (#2963 step 3; Sam's go in session 2026-11-09, "yes, start step 3", on the order Sky set out on #2963). A writer acting without a session: it carries out rulings a reviewer saved on Docket cases (field:kb_curation.docket_ruling). It adds no decision right: each case names the register row that owns its decision (`dr`), the ruling is that owner deciding, and the job runs only the commands the reviewed kb/docket/cases.json names for the choice ruled, only scripts on kb/_docket_process.py's ALLOWED list (each writes committed files it can undo from its own receipt), only with --apply beside --expect. It writes a receipt with its undo under kb/docket/receipts/ and commits to main behind the daily build (concurrency daily-dashboard). Nothing on the decision sheets' hold list reaches it.

dismissed.label: First Light apply
dismissed.why: The First Light tab's Apply (S643; #3153 comments 6826461825 and 6829695812). An hourly look reads one row of first_light_apply_requests before any checkout and ends there when nothing is pending; a pending request or a dispatch turns the reviewers' marks into ONE pull request (selection, hero list, the three views' copies, story photos) and dispatches js-tests.yml on it. No cadence row: no person owns a recurring outcome here, since the run does nothing until a reviewer presses Apply. No new decision right: the workflow never merges, approves or enables auto-merge, so what reaches the views is decided by Sam's merge of the pull request, recorded on GitHub. It holds no student data: painting files, hero photos, and My CPL Story photos MAP already publishes, carried with only the story's link and the name as MAP printed it.

dismissed.label: k=10 disclosure check
dismissed.why: The daily k=10 disclosure check (COBIx security round 1 item 7, #2903, S602). Read-only: it asserts that the two public student rollups suppress every cell under ten and writes nothing; a failure raises one issue through the failure watch (#2905) and the next success closes it. The suppression rule it checks is the student-detail disclosure ADR's, already owned there, so the check adds no decision right and needs no register row.

dismissed.label: Library — publish approved drafts
dismissed.why: Publishes the Library drafts a person approved on their card (Sam, 2026-11-05: "Build it"), every three hours or on dispatch. With the service key it reads only records whose regen carries a draft from the card and an approval (Replace the public copy, or a request to replace at once), writes each draft to library/<slug>/index.html with a receipt of the record's before-values (kb/receipts/library_publish/), commits both to main under the daily-dashboard concurrency group, then moves each record with an update guarded on the updated_at it read, so an edit made on the card since wins. It is the outward step, and it waits on a person's press: the decision to replace a public copy stays with whoever approves the draft, which the record keeps; the workflow only carries it out. Reversible: git revert of the page's commit, and the receipt's before-values (cpl_library_history files the prior row too).

dismissed.label: Program source census
dismissed.why: The program-source census (Phase 0 of the program requirements harvest), weekly. It reads public college websites from a runner under Sam's sheet-23 call 5 (2026-10-03) and writes only program_source_registry, through program_source_census_apply(), which never overwrites a row a person corrected and files every prior row in program_source_registry_history, and (since S326, Sam's go on open-asks sheet 29 card 5) program_source_addenda, through program_source_addenda_apply(), which lists the catalog addenda it sees, marks one gone only after a complete read, never touches a row a person corrected, and files every prior row in program_source_addenda_history. The reading agent (S388) writes the same table through program_source_addenda_read(), service_role only: it moves an addendum from listed to read and files programs_changed from a committed filing in kb/addenda_reads/, never touches a row a person corrected, and leaves every prior row in the history table. It feeds no public surface and carries no staff or student detail. It earns a cadence row when Phase 1 names the person who checks the pilot sample (the lane's open item); a college-facing correction surface goes through Governance before it ships.

dismissed.label: cpl_library
dismissed.why: The Library tab's register of decks, films and documents (Sam, 2026-10-05: build it; files live in the team Drive). Each row is a link and its metadata, never the file. Read and written only under the team phrase or a reviewer sign-in (team_pass_ok() or is_allowed_reviewer()), the same audience as the tab; no anon read, no delete policy, delete and truncate revoked. Every edit files the prior row in cpl_library_history through a trigger, so a write is reversible from the database (Rule 10 a2). It carries no student or staff detail beyond the name a teammate types as added_by or updated_by. Since 2026-10-23 (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 120, cards 2 to 7, each his own call) a row also says who the piece is made for: for_kind (college, district, agency, vendor, the Chancellor's Office, or a typed Other category in for_category) and for_name, an organization's name the title already carries, never a person's; the public read returns them, so the public page can filter by them. The same writers under the same gate, so no new decision right: Make a visual on the tab writes a college's record pair the way the CPL Opportunity side sessions filed the first twelve. Who decides a piece's audience is Sam: a public file with no audience set shows under Needs attention until he rules, so the decision right already has its owner and needs no register row. A second writer, the session-side filer scripts/library_file.py (Sam's calls 7-8, 2026-10-05), records each file it puts in Drive: a receipt applied as a named migration, guarded on the Drive file id so a second apply changes nothing, under updated_by library-filer@bot, with the history trigger keeping the prior row. It writes the link, the version list and home, moves a Requested record to Draft on its first draft and changes no other status, and never sets an audience, so Sam's two decision rights stay his. Since S459 (Sam's Sheet 121 card 1, 2026-10-23) a row also says whether the piece's substance is knowledge and links its KB note (knowledge, kb_note); the same writers under the same gate, no new decision right. Since S490 (Sam, 2026-10-26: "I want to make sure I can Regenerate a visual when I either add a document or note to it") a row also carries the documents a piece is built from (sources: a link, or a document's text a teammate pastes in; the tab's help says never a student's record) and an open rebuild request (regen: who asked, when, whether the draft replaces a public copy at once, the draft's link, who approved it). The same writers under the same gate, and the history trigger files both; replacing a public copy stays the decision of whoever approves the draft on the card, which the request records, so no new decision right.

dismissed.label: cpl_library_pictures
dismissed.why: The pictures a Library piece carries (Sam, 2026-11-11: "the visual didn't include any of the map screenshots from the pdf that the user will need to know how to navigate map", then "just assemble the pics together with the text from the get go"). One row per picture: a screen or figure the Library tab cropped in the browser from a PDF a teammate chose, its page and document, and whether it was left out. Read, added and changed only under the team phrase or a reviewer sign-in (team_pass_ok() or is_allowed_reviewer()), the tab's own audience; no delete policy, a trigger keeps a row's piece and number, and the service role only reads it to publish. Disclosure: a screen can show a person's name or address, so the card shows every picture before publishing with Cover or crop (which rewrites the picture, so the covered part is gone from the row) and Leave it out, Publish it and Replace the public copy wait for a box saying the pictures were checked, and the drafting function names any picture that shows personal details; the tab's help says never a student's record, so the student-detail disclosure ADR does not reach it. No new decision right: what a piece shows stays with whoever asks for it, and publishing with whoever presses Publish it or Replace the public copy, both recorded on the record's regen.

dismissed.label: cpl_reflections
dismissed.why: A journaling surface whose audience is its own authors: written from the First Light page, read only by the weekly digest that goes back to the same team. No third party relies on it, nothing downstream publishes it, and burdening it with decision rights would discourage the writing it exists for. Reversible if the digest ever grows an outside audience. (Sam's ruling, 2026-08-30, the Fifteen Tables.)

dismissed.label: first_light_apply_requests
dismissed.why: The First Light tab's Apply button (same design). One row per request: pending, then stamped by first-light-apply.yml with the pull request it opened or updated. A reviewer sign-in (is_allowed_reviewer()) files a pending row and reads the rows; a trigger blanks every other field on insert, a unique index allows one pending request at a time, and only the service role (the workflow) updates a row; nobody deletes. No new decision right: a request asks for a pull request, and Sam's merge of it is the decision. No student data: a request carries only the requester's sign-in email and the pull request's link.

dismissed.label: first_light_marks
dismissed.why: The First Light tab's marks (Sam, 2026-11-12, #3153: "add a cobi tab so I can edit it"; design #3153 comments 6826461825 and 6829695812). One insert-only row per mark: a painting or photo, keep, drop, add or a position, the collection it came from, and who and when, stamped by trigger from the sign-in. The database numbers each row (an identity column no client can set), and the resolver orders marks by that number, so a reviewer cannot make a mark read as the latest. Read and added only by a reviewer sign-in (is_allowed_reviewer(), the rung of the tab's cobi_nav row); no update or delete is granted to anyone, so a newer mark is the only change and the history stays. A merged Apply records the highest mark it consumed in the committed files, so those marks are spent and a hand edit after the merge stands. No new decision right: a mark changes nothing on its own. The change happens only when Sam merges the pull request that first-light-apply.yml opens from the marks, so the decision stays his merge, recorded on GitHub. Disclosure: no student data. A row names a public-domain painting on Wikimedia Commons, a hero photo already in the repo, or a My CPL Story photo MAP already publishes at map.rccd.edu/cplstories, plus the reviewer's sign-in email, so the student-detail disclosure ADR does not reach it; a Drop mark is the takedown path for a story photo.

dismissed.label: governance_owners
dismissed.why: The register's own annotation layer — it stores who owns the rows on this page. Governed by the register itself; a decision right over the owner column would be circular.
